sources.label: OpenRouter zero-data-retention endpoints (each catalog model has one that supports structured outputs)
OpenRouter API: provider routing and zero data retention

deep.label: Deep
deep.why: Judgment where a mistake is expensive

reasoning.label: Reasoning
reasoning.why: Math, statistics and science-style reasoning; tool use not needed

standard.label: Standard
standard.why: Everyday specialist work that a review step checks

frontier.label: Frontier
frontier.why: The hardest problems only; best quality regardless of price

claude-sonnet-5.5.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
claude-sonnet-5.5.note: Cheapest and fastest model that meets the Deep floor; beats Claude Opus 5.5 on both benchmarks at half the price.

gemini-3.7-flash.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash
gemini-3.7-flash.note: Highest GPQA in the Deep tier at nearly the same cost as Sonnet; a different family, so a good independent reviewer. Slower.

gpt-6.1-sol.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
gpt-6.1-sol.note: Cheapest GPQA-grade reasoning; weaker on multi-turn policy and tool use, so used for statistics and analysis only.

deepseek-v4.1-flash.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
deepseek-v4.1-flash.note: About one-sixth of Sonnet's cost per task for Standard-tier quality; open weights served by many providers.

gpt-6-luna.name: GPT-6 Luna
gpt-6-luna.note: The cheapest model that meets the Fast floor; best for short, single-turn writing.

claude-haiku-5.5.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
claude-haiku-5.5.note: Nearly as cheap as GPT-6 Luna, faster, and better at following procedures over several turns.

gemini-4-argon.name: Gemini 4 Argon
gemini-4-argon.note: Top score on both benchmarks; about three times the cost of Sonnet per task, and slow. Escalation only.

claude-opus-5.5.name: Claude Opus 5.5
claude-opus-5.5.note: Not the primary for any task type: Sonnet 5.5 scored higher on both benchmarks for half the price. Kept for explicit choice.

task_types.name: Strategy and high-stakes decisions
task_types.why: Sonnet is the cheapest model that meets the Deep floor and the fastest; Gemini 3.7 Flash scores higher on GPQA as backup.
task_types.examples: Decision memos, quarterly goals, the monthly report to the Chairman, offer and pricing design

task_types.name: Architecture and technical design
task_types.why: Design mistakes multiply; Deep floor at the lowest price.
task_types.examples: Solution designs, architecture decision records, platform and data architecture, build-versus-buy

task_types.name: Security, legal and compliance review
task_types.why: Careful reading at the Deep floor; Claude runs on the Claude API directly, which keeps sensitive text off third-party routes.
task_types.examples: Threat models, agent safety audits, contract review, risk reviews

task_types.name: QA gates and fact-checks
task_types.why: Highest GPQA in the Deep tier at almost Sonnet's cost, and a different model family from most of the work it reviews.
task_types.examples: Every QA step, estimate and pricing checks, claims in published content

task_types.name: Root-cause analysis and statistics
task_types.why: Cheapest model with GPQA of 0.93 or more; this work needs reasoning, not multi-turn tool use.
task_types.examples: Incident reviews, DMAIC analysis, control charts, measurement system checks

task_types.name: Software and automation build
task_types.why: Standard floor at about one-sixth of Sonnet's cost; escalate security-sensitive code to the Deep tier.
task_types.examples: Features, APIs, agent workflows, data pipelines, tests, infrastructure as code

task_types.name: Infrastructure and production changes
task_types.why: Production work needs Deep-tier care; a cheaper model saves cents and risks an outage.
task_types.examples: Deployment plans, migrations, runbooks, rollback plans

task_types.name: Research and analysis
task_types.why: Long-context reading at the Standard floor for a fraction of the cost; claims still go through a Deep QA gate.
task_types.examples: Market research, competitor matrices, data analysis, financial models, vertical briefs

task_types.name: Client-facing documents
task_types.why: Clients read every word; Deep floor at the lowest price.
task_types.examples: Proposals, SOWs, assessment reports, QBR decks, case studies

task_types.name: Long-form content and training
task_types.why: Good writing at the Standard floor; fact-checks happen at the QA step.
task_types.examples: Articles, newsletters, scripts, curricula, workshop materials

task_types.name: Planning, coordination and communication
task_types.why: Clear, reliable everyday work at the lowest Standard-tier price.
task_types.examples: Routing plans, assignments, schedules, status reports, check-ins, support replies, outreach drafts

task_types.name: Short-form and high-volume content
task_types.why: Many small pieces; GPT-6 Luna is the cheapest model that meets the Fast floor.
task_types.examples: Social posts, captions, hooks, ad variants, titles and meta descriptions, thumbnail text

task_types.name: Routine operations
task_types.why: Templated steps that follow a procedure; Haiku is nearly as cheap as Luna, faster, and better at following procedures.
task_types.examples: Filing records, CRM hygiene, tagging, summaries of long threads, formatting, reminders, monitoring triage

task_types.name: Hardest problems (CEO escalation only)
task_types.why: Top score on both benchmarks; only the orchestrator assigns it, after the Deep tier has not settled the problem.
task_types.examples: A problem the Deep brain has not settled after two passes, or a novel decision with many interacting unknowns

routing.why: The routing plan is a short structured-output judgment over a long, cached team prompt.
